html:
The International Committee of the Red Cross was founded in Geneva in 1863 to care for soldiers wounded in war. It began the worldwide Red Cross movement.

It grew from a book by the Geneva businessman Henry Dunant, who had seen thousands of wounded left without help after the battle of Solferino in 1859. A committee of five Genevans, among them General Dufour of the Sonderbund War, called a conference. In 1864 twelve states signed the first Geneva Convention, which protected the wounded and those who cared for them under the sign of a red cross.

The committee now visits prisoners of war, traces missing people and works in conflicts around the world. National Red Cross and Red Crescent societies exist in almost every country. Its home in Geneva made neutral Switzerland a centre of humanitarian law.
sum: The International Committee of the Red Cross was founded in Geneva in 1863 to care for soldiers wounded in war. It began the worldwide Red Cross movement.
